title: SBOM-Enhanced Threat Correlation for Attack Detection in IoT Networks
content: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices has increased automation and connectivity, but many devices continue to operate with vulnerable or outdated software components, expanding the attack surface. Traditional network-based intrusion detection systems primarily analyse traffic patterns or signatures and may lack information about whether the targeted device contains the software component associated with a detected vulnerability. This limits their ability to provide device-specific context for alert prioritization. This paper proposes an SBOM-informed monitoring and inventory framework that combines software-component vulnerability information with runtime network monitoring for vulnerability-aware threat detection and response. A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is generated for each monitored device and analysed against known Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs). Runtime network traffic is continuously monitored and correlated with the vulnerability context of the corresponding device to identify attack behaviour associated with vulnerable components. The framework further provides automated alerting and remediation guidance based on the correlation results. The prototype was evaluated on a Raspberry Pi testbed using a simulated attack targeting CVE-2015-7855 and compared with a Suricata-based network monitoring baseline. The proposed approach detected the evaluated attack scenarios with zero false positives and required substantially fewer computational resources than the baseline, with mean CPU utilisation of 25.53% compared with 44.83% (43% reduction) and mean memory consumption of 754.8 MB compared with 2467.7 MB (69% reduction). These results indicate the feasibility of SBOM-informed network monitoring for resource-constrained IoT environments.
